pr_title: Watchdog should wait for the worker to shutdown
pr_body:
- Wait for the worker to shutdown
- Increase the default alarm timeout to 15 seconds, but limit the minimum to 10
- Stop extensions and the worker in parallel, so that the time it takes
  to stop them doesn't always fully add up.

Fixes https://github.com/osquery/osquery/issues/7073

The alarm timeout has been increased to a default of 15 seconds which is ample time and should be below the most common services timeout for each platform (last time I checked 20 seconds are the timeout for macOS, other platforms have more).

The minimum limit of 10 seconds is to give some breathing space for the processes to close, especially the worker if it's processing some query. With that limit the worker would actually have 6 seconds to close gracefully and 2 to close brutally/via SIGKILL.
I think that in general to avoid corruption of the DB it's better to leave some time so that the processes can close gracefully.

issue_context.title: Parent process doesn't wait for the worker to exit on shutdown
issue_context.body:
# Bug report

### What operating system and version are you using?

Ubuntu 20.04, Windows 10, macOS 10.15

### What version of osquery are you using?

osquery master (1a7ad4edc6fe0e6b30a50b18b7d7aecff2f04811)

### What steps did you take to reproduce the issue?

This is particularly noticeable due to https://github.com/osquery/osquery/issues/7068.
While testing that bug, I realized that on Linux I would get back the terminal prompt immediately, but the worker would still run in the background and print about its retries.
On Windows, stopping the service is always successful and quick, but the worker keeps running.

This can be therefore easily reproduced with the same flags as the linked bugs,  but maybe with a higher `tls_enroll_max_attempts`
```
--logger_plugin=tls --allow_unsafe --enroll_tls_endpoint=127.0.0.1 --tls_enroll_max_attempts=20
```

### What did you expect to see?

When either the service stops or the CLI returns the terminal prompt, there shouldn't be any other osqueryd processes still running.

### What did you see instead?

osqueryd processes are still running after the service has been stopped or the terminal prompt is back.

This could result in a new osquery instance failing to open the RocksDB database until the worker has exited, after giving a restart to the service.
In general there's the incorrect assumption that osquery fully stopped.

I believe bug #7068 should be fixed first, to provide speed when shutting down.
Also, I think we have a short timeout for the process to exit, after which it exits brutally; I believe this might have to be increased in the presence of a worker still running, maybe ~15 seconds with a warning in the logs when it's hit.
There can be other cases which #7068 won't solve where the worker is doing uninterruptible work (mostly queries), so the timeout should cover this, although brutal.

review_comments: The flag's help says it's the time to wait for graceful, so this oughtn't substract force kill time from it.

The problem is that those 15 seconds are the only time you have to shutdown everything; there's a timer that gets started when shutdown is requested in the main thread, but run on a different thread, which ticks at 15 seconds, and if it hasn't been stopped, then an immediate exit is done.
So there's no time after those 15 seconds, which means that any other part of code has to stay inside that window to close.

What the code is doing then is to leave 2 seconds for the rest of the logic after the watcher shutdown procedure to do a graceful shutdown, and we also account for the fact that killing the child is done in 2 attempts, one where we wait for its graceful shutdown, and the other where we force kill.
Since we don't want to leave zombie processes (because stopChild isn't necessarily used only during shutdown), then we carve out an additional 2 seconds to wait on the process.
I have no opinion what correct is. But the text disagrees with the help comment. Not sure if there's a simple language tweak. This is nit level...

The help comment in the alarm timeout flag is referring to the whole shutdown procedure, which means any process that osquery starts, any internal service that osquery runs.

The other comment you're referring to is in the Watcher, in the code that is killing the child process. The forced kill is referred to the Watcher force killing the child process, which is the second attempt it's doing to stop the child, not the whole osquery package.

This the the 2 seconds I'm referring to:
https://github.com/osquery/osquery/pull/7116/files#diff-976be69b93d9364552ca301a07c92b98a8a9486767f3f546812772a1e81aadbdR394
This is only a portion of the whole shutdown procedure.

Would changing the comment to help a little clarifying things?:
```
/* We leave 2 seconds for the rest of the logic to shutdown, and 2 seconds for the forced kill of the child to do the reaping */
```
I don't think so? The CLI flag says `Seconds to wait for a graceful shutdown.` but I think it's really "Seconds to allow for shutdown", since this also covers a force kill period
oh I see what you mean now, you're right. Yes "Seconds to allow for shutdown" is correct.
